summary: MARSBOUND is an interactive, web-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that introduces students to the challenges of sustaining human life on Mars. Players manage oxygen, water, food, and energy across a 10-Sol mission by making strategic decisions and responding to unexpected events. Through resource management and immediate consequences, the game encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, and an understanding of the engineering trade-offs involved in space exploration. It also introduces real Mars facts sourced from NASA's Mars Fact Sheet.
details:
MARSBOUND – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Your mission. Your decisions. Their survival.

1. Problem

Space exploration involves complex engineering decisions, especially when planning long-duration human missions. Maintaining essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and energy is critical to astronaut survival.

However, these challenges can be difficult for students to understand through traditional learning materials alone. There is a need for an engaging and interactive way to introduce young learners to the resource-management challenges of living on another planet.

2. Our Solution

MARSBOUND is a browser-based educational simulation that allows students to experience the challenges of managing a Mars habitat.

Set in the ARES-VI Habitat at Jezero Crater, Mars, the game places players in charge of maintaining four essential resources: oxygen, water, food, and energy.

Players must make decisions, manage limited supplies, respond to unexpected events, and keep the habitat operational throughout a 10-Sol mission.

3. How It Works

The mission lasts for 10 Martian days (Sols). At the beginning, all four resources start at 100 units.

On each Sol, players choose one of five actions:

  • Improve Radiation Shielding: Uses energy to improve oxygen reserves.
  • Expand Greenhouse: Uses water and energy to increase food supplies.
  • Conserve Energy: Increases energy reserves while consuming some food.
  • Activate Water Recycling: Uses energy to replenish water.
  • Activate Oxygen Generator: Uses water and energy to generate oxygen.

After each decision, daily resource consumption is applied. Oxygen, water, and food decrease by five units each day.

Unexpected events may also occur, including severe dust storms, water system leaks, and temporary solar power surges. These events introduce additional challenges and require players to adapt their decisions.

The mission ends in failure if any resource reaches zero. To successfully complete the mission, players must survive all 10 Sols and maintain the required minimum resource levels.

4. Scientific Context

MARSBOUND incorporates scientific information about Mars from NASA's Mars Fact Sheet.

The landing page introduces three facts:

  • Mean surface gravity: 3.73 m/s².
  • Atmospheric composition: approximately 95.1% carbon dioxide.
  • Length of a Martian day: approximately 24.66 hours.

These facts provide real scientific context for the simulation. The resource values, action effects, random events, and survival thresholds are simplified educational game mechanics rather than official NASA mission specifications.

NASA resource: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html

5. Technology Used

MARSBOUND was developed as a web application using:

  • React
  • JavaScript
  • Vite
  • HTML
  • CSS

The application uses client-side game logic to manage resource updates, player decisions, random events, mission progress, and success or failure conditions.

6. Educational Impact

MARSBOUND aims to make space exploration concepts more accessible and engaging for students.

Through interactive gameplay, learners can:

  • Understand the importance of managing limited resources.
  • Explore the consequences of engineering decisions.
  • Develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Learn basic scientific facts about Mars.
  • Appreciate the challenges involved in sustaining human life beyond Earth.

7. Future Scope

Future improvements could include additional mission scenarios, more realistic habitat challenges, expanded scientific explanations, and new decision-making activities.

MARSBOUND is designed as a starting point for making planetary exploration and space sustainability more interactive and understandable for young learners.

8. Use of AI-Assisted Tools

AI-assisted tools, including ChatGPT and Google Antigravity, were used during project development for brainstorming, planning, coding assistance, debugging, troubleshooting, and documentation. The project implementation was reviewed and tested during development, and the final project decisions and submission were made by the participant.
